Perform no DNS resolution or fetching and preserve accepted input exactly.

Generate eight-character base62 codes using SecureRandom.nextInt(62). Attempt insertion at most five times, retrying only PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 23505 violations identifying the named code uniqueness constraint. Avoid wrapping the retry loop in a transaction that becomes aborted after a collision.

Add a new V1 migration only after confirming that version is unoccupied and its path is allowed. Create url_service and url_service.urls with an identity primary key, a named unique code constraint, text destination, timestamptz creation/access timestamps, and bigint click_count defaulting to zero with a nonnegative check.

Resolve redirects with one UPDATE url_service.urls SET click_count = click_count + 1, last_accessed_at = clock_timestamp() WHERE code = ? RETURNING url statement. Do not perform a separate read or application-side increment.

Bind the existing shortener.public-base-url property in a new Java configuration component. Validate it at startup as an absolute HTTP/HTTPS origin without credentials, query, fragment, or a non-root path; normalize its trailing slash. Build shortUrl by appending /r/{code}, independently of request and forwarding headers.

POST /api/urls returns 201 with code, shortUrl, url, and createdAt. GET /r/{code} returns 302 with the exact stored destination as Location. Analytics returns code, url, createdAt, clickCount, and nullable lastAccessedAt.

Use centralized exception handling for invalid input (400), unknown codes (404), and allocation exhaustion or persistence failures (controlled 500). Do not expose SQL, credentials, or internal exception messages.
Return Cache-Control: no-store on redirects so clients and intermediaries are instructed to contact the service for each tracked redirect.
Exclude expiration and rate limiting despite their existing configuration properties. Keep analytics reads free of counter mutations.

Use existing JUnit 5 and Spring test facilities for unit and HTTP contract tests; reserve PostgreSQL-specific migration, collision identification, persistence, and concurrency verification for the trusted runner.

# URL service baseline

POST /api/urls accepts {"url":"https://example.invalid/path"} and returns 201 with code, shortUrl, url, and createdAt. GET /r/{code} returns 302 with the exact stored destination and Cache-Control: no-store. GET /api/urls/{code}/analytics returns code, url, createdAt, clickCount, and lastAccessedAt. New records have zero clicks and a null access timestamp. Unknown codes return 404, invalid requests return 400, and allocation or database failures return a sanitized 500.

Destinations are validated using URI parsing without DNS resolution or fetching. Accepted values are preserved. Credentials, control characters, malformed authorities, invalid ports, and non-HTTP/HTTPS schemes are rejected.

Set SHORTENER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the externally reachable local HTTP/HTTPS origin. Its existing default is http://127.0.0.1:8000; Java defaults to port 8080, so routing or an explicit origin setting must reconcile them. Credentials, queries, fragments, and non-root paths are prohibited. Forwarding headers never determine generated links.

Codes contain eight ASCII base62 characters generated with SecureRandom. Creation makes at most five independent insertion attempts, retrying only SQLSTATE 23505 with structured constraint metadata naming urls_code_unique. PostgreSQL is an existing runtime-only dependency, so metadata access uses reflection and fails closed. There is no encompassing allocation transaction. All repository SQL qualifies url_service.urls. Redirect resolution increments click_count and sets last_accessed_at in one UPDATE ... RETURNING statement. Counts measure database resolutions, not proof that clients received or followed redirects.

The existing V1 migration creates url_service and its initial table. Preserve that migration; do not replace it. Expiration and rate limiting are excluded from the explicit baseline requirement. Existing configuration values do not activate these behaviors.

## Trusted-runner test evidence

The supplied revision 1 runner result, dated 2026-10-14, exited with code 1. Gradle completed compileJava and bootJar, then failed at compileTestJava while resolving testCompileClasspath. Offline mode could not resolve the uncached existing transitive dependency org.apiguardian:apiguardian-api:1.1.2. The result reports zero executed tests and no test suites. The gate requiring at least one executed JUnit test therefore remains unsatisfied. Successful production compilation and jar creation do not establish runtime correctness.

This is a runner dependency-cache blocker. Provision the existing declared dependency graph through the approved trusted-runner process, then rerun Gradle test inside the trusted Docker runner. Do not change manifests, add dependencies, replace JUnit with stubs, weaken acceptance gates, or execute generated code on the host.

Existing JUnit tests use Mockito repository/code-generator doubles and standalone Spring MVC. They do not establish PostgreSQL behavior or live HTTP success. No passing JUnit result was supplied. No results were supplied for Python tests, frontend typecheck/build, or independent HTTP acceptance checks.

## Live-run evidence

No successful live-run evidence was supplied. Unit tests and MVC tests using doubles must not be reported as live runs.

## Remaining verification

Before applying this documentation replacement, the orchestrator must confirm its path is permitted by orchestrator/workspaces.py. Preserve manifests, application.yml, the starter application, existing migrations, and protected acceptance checks.

The trusted Docker runner must execute Python tests, frontend typecheck/build, Java tests, and the independent HTTP acceptance checks. Document every omitted check and its reason. Do not provision cloud services.

Using real PostgreSQL, verify V1 on an empty database, named uniqueness and nonnegative counter constraints, table access with a search_path excluding url_service, collision classification and recovery, and persistence across service restart. Create a URL and confirm zero/null initial analytics. Issue N concurrent redirects with automatic following disabled; require all N responses to be 302 with the exact stored Location, a count increase of exactly N, and a non-null access timestamp. Verify another code is unaffected and analytics reads do not mutate counters or access timestamps. Verify destination validation generates no outbound traffic.

Record sanitized runner results separately for tests using doubles, PostgreSQL integration checks, and live HTTP runs. Never record credentials, runtime databases, or raw provider logs.

Return code and shortUrl from creation with status 201. Persist in PostgreSQL using JdbcTemplate and a Flyway migration. Validate HTTP/HTTPS destinations without fetching them, reject credentials/control characters, use cryptographically random base62 codes with bounded unique-conflict retries, and count concurrent redirects atomically. Add JUnit tests. No expiration or rate limiting in this baseline.
